slides: Welcome back. Now three special cases from the exam. Trains that have a length, boats on a river, and circular tracks.

slides.say: The formula stays the same. Distance is equal to speed times time. Only the distance, or the speed, is different.

slides: In this lesson we learn the trains and the circular tracks. The river comes in its own question.

slides.say: Until now, every traveler was a dot. But a train is not a dot. It has a length.
Now a new example. A train two hundred meters long passes a post, at twenty-five meters a second. How long does that take?
at: A train two hundred meters long
A train two hundred meters long

slides.say: The train starts passing when its front reaches the post. It finishes when its back passes the post.
at: It finishes when its back passes

slides.say: So the front moves exactly one train length, two hundred meters. Past a post, the train covers its own length.
at: Past a post, the train covers its own length

slides.say: The time is the distance divided by the speed. Two hundred divided by twenty-five is eight seconds.

slides: Now a second example, from a real exam. A train passes a man on a platform at a hundred twenty kilometers per hour. It takes half a minute. How long is the train?

slides.say: A hundred twenty kilometers in sixty minutes is two kilometers every minute.
In half a minute, the train moves one kilometer.
Passing a man is like passing a post. So the distance it moves is its own length. The train is one kilometer long.
at: The train is one kilometer long

slides.say: Now a bridge. The same train, two hundred meters long, at twenty-five meters a second, crosses a bridge three hundred meters long completely.
It starts when the front gets on the bridge.
at: It starts when the front gets on

slides.say: And it ends when the back gets off the bridge.
at: it ends when the back gets off

slides.say: So the front moves across the whole bridge, and then one more train length. A bridge means the bridge plus the train.
at: A bridge means the bridge plus the train

slides.say: Three hundred plus two hundred is five hundred meters.
Five hundred divided by twenty-five is twenty seconds.
A lot of students divide only the bridge, three hundred divided by twenty-five, twelve seconds. That forgets the train's own length.

slides: A platform or a tunnel works the same way as a bridge. Its length, plus the train. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
